app.title: Genetic Ancestry Visualization (ezancestry Streamlit app)
app.summary: The person picks a published panel of ancestry-informative markers and a population resolution (continental or regional). Then they upload one person's raw genotype file. The app reduces the genotypes to the panel's markers and projects them into the same principal-component space as a labelled reference cohort. A 3D scatter plot shows the new sample as a large black point among the reference samples, which are coloured by population. Below the plot are the population a nearest-neighbour classifier predicts and its probability for each population. The marker genotypes of the uploaded sample and of the reference cohort can also be shown as tables.

task.text: Place one individual's genotypes among a labelled reference cohort and predict which population they most resemble, with a probability for each population.

data.text: A reference cohort of individuals genotyped at a fixed panel of marker SNPs and labelled by population and superpopulation, plus one uploaded raw genotype file (consumer genotyping export or VCF) reduced to the same markers.
data.item: an individual's genotypes at the panel's marker SNPs

stage.text: inferring an individual's ancestry from raw genotype data against a reference panel

mechanism.text: Sidebar radios choose the marker panel and population resolution, and a file uploader brings in one sample. Each change re-runs a one-hot, PCA and k-nearest-neighbour pipeline. The 3D scatter of the first three components places the sample among the reference cohort, coloured by population. A text line gives the predicted label and a one-row table gives the class probabilities. Checkboxes reveal the raw genotype tables.

field.text: PCA projection and nearest-neighbour ancestry inference from marker SNPs in population genetics

workflow.name: classify a new sample against a labelled reference set

steps.step: choose the reference scheme and the level of detail
steps.here: Sidebar radios pick the 55-marker or 128-marker published panel and continental (superpopulation) or regional (population) resolution; the reference cohort is drawn at once.
A file uploader takes a raw genotype file. The snps library parses it, and it is merged onto the panel's marker list, so any marker missing from the file stays empty.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A pretrained pipeline (one-hot encoding, PCA, distance-weighted kNN) runs on both the reference cohort and the new sample, giving three PCA coordinates and class probabilities for each.

steps.step: compare the new item against the reference groups
steps.here: A rotatable 3D scatter of PC1–PC3 colours and shapes the reference samples by population and shows the uploaded sample as a large black point.

steps.step: read the predicted class and its confidence
steps.here: A text line names the predicted population, and a one-row table lists the probability for each population at the chosen resolution.
Checkboxes show the uploaded sample's genotypes at the panel markers and the full reference genotype table.

distinctive: The person can switch between two published marker panels of different sizes, and each panel has its own pretrained model.
The person can switch between two population resolutions (continental or regional), and the plot's colours and the probability columns follow the choice.
The new sample is projected into a space fitted on the reference cohort, so it is judged by where it sits among the labelled groups.
Raw consumer genotype exports are read directly, and markers the file lacks are left missing rather than refused.
